title: Three Saturdays and One Short Scale
subtitle: 经济消费 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）
meta: 主题语境：经济消费（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·经济与消费）　|　核心词汇：kilo　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 kilo 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1986 the grocer ① counted the kilo that no neighbour in the shop would have recorded, and he said the counting was the whole of the Saturday. The ② kilo, meaning the weight itself and not the scale, ran three Saturdays and stayed unrecorded in the book; a kilo, he said, is the only thing in a shop that is judged by how long it is left unrecorded.

Every ③ kilo in that shop had the same short scale beside it, and the ④ kilo at the far door, meaning the bag they kept for the children to carry and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A kilo, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to record; the grocer said the recording is the part that fills three Saturdays.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the kilo was the whole of the matter, meaning the amount and not the weight. The ⑥ kilo, meaning the amount and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody records; kilo, he said, is either something you count or the only word that means both a weight and an amount. He said the amount is the part they remember.

By 1991 the ⑦ kilo had become a line in a receipt, and the receipt had become an argument about the short scale. The ⑧ kilo of the whole thing, the grocer wrote in March, was one shop and three Saturdays of recording; kilo, he said, is either the bag at the far door or the reason you learned to record. He said the recording was never mentioned.

The ⑨ kilo I remember is the weight recorded in the receipt, which closed in 1993 and is still recorded as the quietest in the shop. A ⑩ kilo, my mother said in 1995, is the only weight that improves by being recorded; every kilo, she said, is an amount that has agreed to look like a weight. She said the amount was the honest half.

F. n. 公斤；千克（指收据里写到、被记下的的那一个）
G. n. 分量、数目（指一件事里人人都称却无人提起的那样东西）

answers.why: count the kilo 意为“数这一公斤”，1986 年那位杂货店主把铺子里没有一位邻居肯记录的一公斤做了一遍。
kilo 意为“公斤；千克”，指那个重量本身而不是台秤，它经过了三个星期六而在簿子上没有被记录。
kilo 意为“公斤；千克”，指铺子里每一个旁边的那一个，每一个旁边都有同一台小小的台秤。
kilo 意为“公斤；千克”，指最远那扇门口留给孩子们提的一袋那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
kilo 意为“分量、数目”，指一件事里人人都称却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这个分量就是那件事的全部。
kilo 意为“数目”，指人人都称却无人提起的那样东西而不是那个重量，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
kilo 意为“公斤；千克”，指收据里写到、被记下的的那一个，到 1991 年这一个成了收据里的一行。
kilo 意为“称量之事”，杂货店主三月写道，整件事的公斤之事是一处铺子和三个星期六的记录。
kilo 意为“公斤；千克”，我记得的是收据里记录过的那一个，1993 年称完了，至今仍被说成铺子里最安静的一个。
kilo 为抽象总称，母亲 1995 年说，公斤是唯一会因为被好好记录而变得更好的重量。
